status: mailbox-only cache delay fixed; established-stream stalls and 180-second large-file failure remain open

controlled_defect.description: A positive general rendezvous cache containing only mailbox ads hid a newly available signed stream ad until its ordinary 15-second TTL expired.
controlled_defect.fixture: Real NodeRuntime/NodeServices, independently signed ads in separate DHT slots, new stream slot introduced after the initial mailbox-only lookup. Rechecked after 1.1 seconds, inside the ordinary TTL.
controlled_defect.correction: Stream resolution treats a mailbox-only set as a one-second cached miss. A usable stream set and ordinary callers retain the existing TTL. Known identity mailbox cookie at a device address is excluded as well as the device-derived mailbox cookie.
controlled_defect.concurrency_evidence: Eight same-recipient waiters share one refreshed full-slot query batch. Eight immediate retries before the miss expires add no network walks. Signed ad validation, expiry filtering and per-recipient locking remain in force.
other_use_controls: Mailbox routes are not removed on stream miss.
Last-known valid deposit fallback remains available until expiry or explicit eviction.
Expired stream ads cannot make a mailbox-only set stream-ready.
Ordinary send/deposit and refresh-ahead callers retain their prior cache modes.

limits: The lower sampled local wait and lack of discovery misses in this WAN run do not establish a universal speed improvement or isolate the cache correction from path variation.
The reverse 32-MiB transfer failed the unchanged 180-second gate. A prior successful run on the previous SDK does not qualify this run, and a regression is not ruled out by unit tests.
The first 4-MiB upload retried after a source application-progress timeout; the transfer passed final integrity only after retry.
Driver summaries are event-driven samples, not absolute maxima or RTT measurements.
No calls, camera, audio playout, Windows reproduction or full multi-device qualification in this cycle.
privacy: Aggregate values only: no endpoint identifiers, addresses, paths, keys, packet sequences, raw captures or file hashes.
